applicant_utility.summary: With roughly 25 awards against more than a thousand applicants, the LExS is a lottery you enter with a 500-word motivation letter inside your admission application, not a standalone funding plan. The award covers only part of tuition (between EUR 10,000 and EUR 19,000 depending on the level granted) and explicitly requires a significant personal contribution, so non-EEA recipients must still prove sufficient funds for the residence permit. The scholarship section only becomes visible after you submit your admission application, so leaving the admission file late is the fastest way to lose the option entirely.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Academically outstanding non-EEA/non-EFTA applicants to an eligible September-start Leiden master's who can still fund the remainder themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Create and submit the admission application first; the LExS only appears in the Scholarships section afterwards
Allow up to three working days for the application to be created or submitted before the deadline
Draft the motivation letter to the 500-word PDF limit and finalise it before 1 December 2026
If applying to more than one programme or specialisation, prepare a separate LExS application and letter inside each admission application
Check whether you also hold a full external scholarship; combining it with the LExS is not possible and must be notified
common_rejection_risks: Discovering the LExS was not visible because the admission application was never submitted or was late
Applying to a non-advanced LLM or MSc at Leiden Law School, or to a February-start programme, which are excluded
Already holding a Leiden master's degree without a mandatory-previous-programme exception
Emailing extra documents after submission; the page states no changes or additions are possible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, insurance, travel and the remaining tuition above the granted level are all yours; non-EEA recipients must show proof of sufficient funds for the visa/residence permit regardless of the award.
document_audit: The motivation letter is capped at 500 words in PDF; a longer file is an avoidable own goal
UK nationals who registered in the Dutch BRP before 1 January 2021 are excluded despite the UK being non-EEA
The award level is final and non-negotiable once granted, so do not negotiate after selection
alerts: Late scholarship applications are not considered under any circumstances
The top 10% indication is not verified with proof of ranking; it signals competitiveness only
All applicants hear the outcome by email before the end of March, whether successful or not
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the admission application, reopen the Apply screen, open Scholarships, select the LExS, upload the 500-word motivation letter, submit before 1 December 2026, then wait for the faculty decision by the end of March.

applicant_utility.summary: Groningen's version of the NL Scholarship is a single EUR 5,000 payment in your first year, aimed at living costs rather than tuition, and you can only apply after you already hold an admission offer for one of the programmes on the published list. That sequencing is the trap: the scholarship clock starts only when the admission letter exists, so it rewards applicants who applied for admission early. The award can be received only once in a lifetime, and the university plainly states the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA students holding an admission offer for a listed Groningen master's with a strong, well-documented undergraduate record.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme appears on the applicable-programmes list before counting on this award
Apply for admission as early as possible; the scholarship application only opens once you have the (conditional) offer
Write the motivation letter to connect your academic goals with studying in the Netherlands and your future plans, since that is what the committee weighs
Prepare a transcript of records covering all undergraduate courses so far, not just final-year results
Upload every required document in one go; incomplete applications are excluded from consideration
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a programme that is not on the applicable-programmes list
Any prior Dutch education or diploma, including non-exchange prior study, which breaks eligibility
Submitting an incomplete file, which is automatically excluded
Holding an EU/EEA fee rate for any other reason, which disqualifies you even if your passport is non-EEA
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, insurance, travel and most living costs remain yours; the university states living and study costs are not covered by this grant, so the EUR 5,000 is a first-year contribution only.
document_audit: A conditional admission letter is acceptable at application, but the offer itself must be for a listed programme
The transcript must cover all undergraduate courses so far, not a summary or a degree certificate alone
Exchange programmes in the Netherlands are excluded from the no-previous-Dutch-education rule, but degree study is not
alerts: One award per lifetime; a second application in a later year is not possible
The university aims to notify all applicants by 15 March and no further action is needed from applicants
Check the page before the next cycle: the 2027-2028 deadline had not been published at verification
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Receive an admission offer for a listed programme, complete the online NL Scholarship application form, upload the motivation letter, transcript and admission letter before the February deadline, then await the faculty decision by email around mid-March.
